newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann files complaint against Telekom.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann files complaint against Telekom.

text.p: Mannesmann Arcor AG, the German telecommunications group, said on Monday that it had filed a complaint with the government against Deutsche Telekom AG as interconnection negotiations were producing no result.

Mannesmann's complaint comes just after another Telekom rival, O.Tel.O of utilities Veba AG and RWE AG, filed a similar complaint. The government will now have to intervene and set interconnection tariffs.

Mannesmann Arcor said in a statement that in interconnection negotiations with Deutsche Telekom it was not able to come to a satisfactory agreement on terms of access to lines that connect homes and offices to local switches.
"Without such access Arcor would not have access to a considerable potential to market its own telephone services," the company said in a statement.
"Mannesmann Arcor expects the regulatory agency to order Deutsche Telekom by April 30, 1997, at the latest to put forward a negotiable offer for use of its direct access lines," it added.
Because Deutsche Telekom as former monopoly is the only phone company with access to virtually every home and business in Germany, its new rivals must lease its lines to gain access to customers.

Dubbed interconnection in industry jargon, these agreements form the cost basis for Telekom's rivals and without clarity over interconnection tariffs they cannot plan their networks or calculate their costs.
Most European Union countries, including Germany, will open their telecoms markets to full competition in January. Such interconnection agreements must be in place before then.
